new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (4 pp., text present; the PDF's metadata: 'Microsoft Word - Ata_ata (Unicode Compliant)', produced 2013 by SIL 'lr-webpub'). Running `extracted text` on the PDF gives, at page 3 lines 19-20, exactly: 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' / 'Stress is predictable and falls on the second last syllable.' -- verbatim as quoted, at the stated locator. Surrounding context read: p.1 header 'Organised Phonology Data / Ata (Pele Ata, Wasi) Language [ATA] / Kimbe - West New Britain Province / East Papuan Phylum; New Britain Stock; Pele Ata Family-Level Isolate / Population census: 1900 (1980) / Major villages: Malasi, Sale, Sexe, Uasilau, Sipa, Kaikou / Linguistic work done by: SIL /…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and fixed on the penultimate syllable. (Vowel length is phonemic and independent of stress: /a aa e ee i ii o oo u uu/.)
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned; the OPD gives no discussion of long vowels/diphthongs vs. syllable count for stress placement.
new_statements.domain_note: Standard SIL OPD one-line statement; implicitly the (citation-form) word. No phrase-level discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD describes 'Ata (Pele Ata, Wasi)' as spoken around Kimbe, West New Britain (villages Malasi, Sale, Sexe, Uasilau, Sipa, Kaikou, i.e. both the Lower/Pele and Upper/Ata dialect areas); it is the language-level pele1245 [ata], no dialect split made for the stress statement.
